newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta shares end down on ITC travails.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta shares end down on ITC travails.

text.p: Share prices continued to come under renewed pressures and closed lower at the Calcutta Stock Exchange (CSE) on Wednesday despite mild mid-session short covering, brokers said.
They said that nervousness over investigations of financial irregularities by ITC Ltd and selling pressures prompted other blue-chips to edge down in sympathy.

Brokers said that even the higher than expected backwardation charge on ITC shares at the close of the last accounting period averaging four rupees per share failed to force the short sellers on the defensive.

"The stock markets look very bad. The fall in prices is not nearing the bottom as yet," said Rishi Dhanuka of brokers Ratnabali Securities Limited. "Foreign institutional investors are still not buying anything indicating that they expect prices to fall further."

"I expect the foreign funds to return as buyers after December when prices of blue-chips would have fallen to rock bottom levels. Till such time the investors will continue to lack confidence to buy any scrips," Dhanuka added.

Brokers said that while several foreign funds were selling against deliveries, large lots were being sold on a speculative basis and this explained the sustained high backwardation charge on several scrips including ITC.
